title: Old Parish Records — shared Stage B definitions
description: Single source of truth for definitions reused by every Stage B record schema (source citation, place identification, period jurisdiction, aliases, vital status, previous spouse, extra participants). Record schemas carry IDENTICAL copies under their own $defs (so each validates standalone with `jsonschema -i`); tools/sync_shared_defs.py copies them in and --check verifies they have not drifted. Edit here, then run the sync.

source_citation.description: Where the entry can be seen. All parts nullable: existing records have no URL yet. matricula_url is the canonical image-page permalink (viewer URL with ?pg=N), not the hosted-images JPEG.

matricula_url.description: Canonical Matricula viewer permalink to the image page, e.g. https://data.matricula-online.eu/en/deutschland/aachen/lank-st-stephanus/KB+999_3/?pg=2. Copy from the entry manifest matricula_url when present.

citation.description: Human-readable citation, e.g. 'Lank, St. Stephanus, Trauungen KB 999_3, scan KB_999-118, p. 252, entry 4. Matricula Online: <url>'.

archive.description: Holding archive as Matricula names it (e.g. 'Aachen, rk. Bistum'; 'Erzbistumsarchiv Paderborn').

matricula_collection.description: Matricula collection / parish code when the URL uses one (e.g. DE_EBAP_22212); null for slug URLs.

parish.description: Parish display name (e.g. 'Lank St. Stephanus'). The machine key stays parish_slug.

book_signature.description: Book signature as shown on Matricula (e.g. 'KB 999_3', 'KB005-02-H'). Usually = archival_id.

image_label.description: Matricula image label when known (e.g. KB_999-118).

page.description: Printed page / folio as cited (usually = page).

accessed.description: Date the URL was checked (ISO YYYY-MM-DD).

place_identification.description: A place as written vs the identified real place. Superset of opr-place-ref v1.0.0 (places/place_ref.schema.json): residence_as_written is called place_as_written here because the same object is used for marriage_place / burial_place; place_id, as_of_date, match_confidence and notes are identical.

place_as_written.description: Place words as in transcription_latin (diplomatic: abbreviations, periods, [?] kept), without the governing preposition (ex / in / de) unless it is part of the name. E.g. 'Schall.', 'Berenbrok', 'Lanck ven Lüten'.

identified_name.description: Editorial/normalized name of the identified place (e.g. Schallern, Klieve). null when not identified.

place_id.description: Gazetteer id from /workspace/lank-schema/places/ (opr-place.place_id, e.g. place:lank). null until the place exists in the gazetteer.

as_of_date.description: Event date (ISO) used to pick time-bounded names/admin rows from the gazetteer.

basis.description: Why this identification (e.g. 'written in full', 'project identification', 'abbreviation of the groom's residence').

admin_level.description: Use the opr-place-admin admin_level vocabulary (herrschaft, amt, kreis, departement, state, country, deanery, …). Proposed additions pending Stephen: territory, diocese.

period_jurisdiction.description: Historical territory / Amt / diocese at the time of the event. The temporal gazetteer (places/place_admin.schema.json) is the source of truth: prefer source=gazetteer with place_id + as_of_date and resolve admin rows at query time (nothing is copied). source=editorial is a stop-gap snapshot for places not yet in the gazetteer; promote it into place_admin rows later.

place_id.description: Gazetteer place whose place_admin rows apply (event place, else residence, else parish seat).

editorial_levels.description: Only when source=editorial. Ordered broad → narrow or as known.

basis.description: Which place the jurisdiction was resolved for (e.g. 'parish seat', 'event place').

alias.description: One byname / alias of a person.

form.description: Alias in person-field form (capitalized, nominative), e.g. Schäper, Herweg, Brauns.

marker.description: Normalized marker lemma: dictus (dictus/dicta/dtā/dtʸ/dæ̱), genannt (gen./genannt), vulgo (vulgo/vulg.), condictus (cond./condictus/conducta/condicta), alias, other.

form_as_written.description: Alias as written when it differs from form (case, lowercase, [?]).

person_aliases.description: Map person field name → aliases of that person. The person field keeps the primary name only. Each record schema restricts the keys to its own person fields.

vital_status.description: Whether a named person (usually a parent) is stated to be dead at the time of the event, plus the words that say so.

status.description: deceased: defunctus/defuncti/Ffti/obitorum/selig/sel./†/p.m.; living: explicitly stated; uncertain: ambiguous wording (e.g. quondam = formerly or late).

as_written.description: Diplomatic word(s) from transcription_latin that carry the status (e.g. 'Ffti', 'obtōrum', 'quondam', 'selig'). For a couple-level word ('obtōrum Cjgūm') repeat it on both parents.

previous_spouse.description: Earlier spouse of a widowed bride/groom (or of the deceased).

name.description: Nominative person-field form; keep [?] and N.

name_as_written.description: Diplomatic form from transcription_latin (e.g. genitive 'Marie Margarethae Schüer[?]').

person_with_residence.description: Extra named participant (witness / sponsor) beyond the fixed slots, with residence.

notes.description: Role/title as written (e.g. 'Custos in Horn'), kinship, marks.
